decision.expected_information_gain: Determine whether the current accepted four-symbol data surface supports a precise cross-market lead-lag identity without spending a V2 attempt or requesting additional market data.

implementation_semantics.interpretation: Use the result only to decide whether a prospectively frozen lead-lag methodology has adequate causal timestamp support; any later outer requires a separately frozen specification and independent unopened data.

screen.observation_rule: Use only timestamps where the source and target have broker-native rows at the required consecutive timestamps; exclude gaps, sessions without rows, incomplete windows, synthetic fills, and forward fills.
outputs: source-direction to target-next-bar direction contingency tables

next_research_state.required_interpretation: Assess structural sufficiency and dependence diagnostics only; if sufficient, freeze a finite lead-lag methodology prospectively before considering any independent outer.

objective.goal: Materialize the smallest non-economic cross-market lead-lag prerequisite screen on the accepted AUDJPY, AUS200, Brent-F, and BCHUSD M5 capture.
objective.information_gain_rationale: The accepted disjoint capture provides 9,233 strict five-timestamp windows across 79 contiguous segments and complete pairwise overlap for all twelve ordered pairs. This is sufficient to evaluate whether causal one-bar lag availability and directional contingency are structurally usable, while avoiding new data, stale outer reuse, economic outcomes, or premature family closure.
